 EX-99.1 Q2 2027 EARNINGS RELEASE
 Exhibit 99.1 
 NEWS RELEASE 
 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
 MiniMed Delivers Strong Fiscal Q2 with Accelerating Pump Demand, Expanding Profitability, and Faster Pipeline Commercialization 
 NORTHRIDGE, Calif., November 24, 2026 – MiniMed (Nasdaq: MMED) today reported financial results for its second quarter (Q2) of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), ended October 30, 2026. 
 • Accelerating pump demand supports durable growth: New Pumps Sold (NPS) increased 18% year-over-year, accelerating from 8% in Q1 
 • Broad-based growth across geographies: U.S. net sales grew 8%, with NPS >30%; International net sales grew 10% as reported and 10% organic, with Western Europe NPS increasing >20% 
 • Operating rigor driving profitability and cash generation: Net Income at 3% of sales, Adjusted EBITDA margin of 17%; operating cash flow of $116 million ; free cash flow of $55 million , positive for the first time as an independent company 
 • Post-quarter pipeline commercialization advances rapidly: MiniMed Fit™ FDA cleared in under three months, several months early, accelerating U.S. launch from Summer to Spring 2027; MiniMed Flex™ with Simplera™ launched last week in Western Europe; MiniMed Flex™ with Instinct, made by Abbott, received CE Mark with launch planned in Q4 FY27 
 “MiniMed delivered another strong quarter, with consistent execution across our business, accelerating pump demand, improving profits and cash generation, and continued momentum in our innovation pipeline,” said MiniMed Chief Executive Officer Que Dallara. “New Pumps Sold growth accelerated to 18% worldwide, reinforcing the strength of demand for our products, and our confidence in durable revenue growth. With MiniMed Flex™ expanding internationally and MiniMed Fit™ receiving FDA clearance ahead of expectations, we are adding important new drivers across our portfolio. We believe this progress positions us well for the next phase of MiniMed’s growth.” 
 Q2 Results 
 • Worldwide net sales of $822 million grew 9.4% as reported and 9.7% organic, including an approximately $(3) million impact from foreign currency translation 
 ◦ International net sales of $579 million grew 9.8% as reported and 10.4% organic, supported by new product introductions, increased sensor availability, and continued AID adoption; Western Europe NPS increased >20% 
 ◦ U.S. net sales of $243 million grew 8.3% as reported and organic. NPS increased >30%, driven by the continued expansion of the MiniMed Flex™ launch 
 ◦ Worldwide pump net sales of $151 million grew 14.7% as reported and 15.0% organic 
 ◦ Worldwide CGM net sales of $423 million grew 10.4% as reported and 10.8% organic 
 ◦ Worldwide consumables net sales of $243 million grew 4.0% as reported and 4.6% organic 
 • GAAP net income was $22 million or 2.6% of sales; Adjusted EBITDA was $140 million or 17.0% margin 
 • Worldwide NPS of ~38,000, an increase of 18.3% year over year 
 • Worldwide CGM Attachment Rate of 70%, an increase of ~100 bps quarter over quarter 
 1 
 Recent Highlights 
 • MiniMed Fit™ FDA clearance creates an important new growth opportunity with a first-of-its-kind tubeless experience. Combines up to seven days of uninterrupted wear without charging or cartridge changes, 300-unit insulin capacity, SmartGuard™ automation, and compatibility with Simplera™ and Instinct 
 • MiniMed Flex™ international expansion provides another near-term growth catalyst. MiniMed Flex™ with Simplera™ launched in Europe last week; MiniMed Flex™ with Instinct, made by Abbott, received CE Mark and expected to launch in Q4 FY27 
 • DGK (dual glucose-ketone) sensor, made by Abbott, expected to launch with MiniMed™ Flex and MiniMed™ Fit in Summer 2027 
 FY27 Outlook 
 For the fiscal year 2027 ending April 30, 2027, MiniMed expects: 
 • Organic revenue growth of approximately 10.5%, reaffirming prior guidance. The outlook includes the approximate 1.0 to 1.5% benefit from the extra week in Q1 FY27; and 
 • Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 11.3%, reaffirming the guidance updated following FDA clearance of MiniMed Fit™ solely to reflect the accelerated $162 million Blackstone charge. Excluding this expected charge, MiniMed’s underlying adjusted EBITDA margin outlook remains unchanged at approximately 16%, consistent with the outlook in effect immediately before Fit clearance. 
 MiniMed’s strong Q2 performance provides capacity to fund the manufacturing, sales, and marketing investments being pulled forward to support the accelerated MiniMed Fit™ launch while maintaining the company’s fiscal 2027 outlook. 
 Conference Call Details 
 MiniMed will host a conference call at 5:30 a.m. Pacific Standard Time (PST) today, Tuesday, November 24, 2026, to discuss its second quarter financial results. The live audio webcast will be available on the Investor Relations section of MiniMed's website at investors.minimed.com . Within 24 hours of the webcast, an archived replay will be available for a minimum of 12 months following the call. 
 Investor Second Quarter Earnings Presentation 
 An investor presentation providing additional information and analysis on fiscal second quarter results and guidance can be found on the Investor Relations section of MiniMed’s website at investors.minimed.com . 
 Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
 In addition to our financial results determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP, we present in this earnings press release certain financial measures that facilitate management’s review of the operational performance and liquidity of MiniMed and serve as a basis for strategic planning. However, such financial measures are not presented in our financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. These financial measures are considered “non-GAAP financial measures” and are intended to supplement, and should not be considered superior to, financial measures presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. This includes Organic Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin and Free Cash Flow. We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide information useful to investors in understanding our underlying operational performance, liquidity, trends and our ability to generate cash from operations after investments in property, plant and equipment and may facilitate comparisons with the performance of other companies in the medical technologies industry. 
 2 
 In particular, we believe that the use of Organic Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, and Free Cash Flow is helpful to our investors as they are metrics used by management to assess the health of our business and our operating performance and liquidity. However, non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental informational purposes only, has limitations as an analytical tool, and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP measures differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial measures as tools for comparison. 
 In the tables included at the end of this earnings press release, a reconciliation is provided for each historical non-GAAP financial measure included in this release to the most directly comparable financial measure stated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. 
 MiniMed calculates forward-looking Organic Revenue Growth and Adjusted EBITDA margin, which are non-GAAP financial measures, based on internal forecasts that omit certain amounts that would be included in GAAP financial measures. MiniMed does not provide a reconciliation of forward-looking Non-GAAP measures to the comparable GAAP measure because certain items cannot be reasonably predicted without unreasonable effort. Such items could have a substantial impact on GAAP measures of financial performance. 
 Forward-Looking Statements 
 This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, which are subject to risks and uncertainties, including risks related to the Company’s ability to realize the benefits of its separation from Medtronic plc (“Medtronic”), the risk of disruption or unanticipated costs in connection with the Company’s separation from Medtronic, the Company’s ability to succeed as a standalone publicly traded company, competitive factors, difficulties and delays inherent in the development, manufacturing, marketing and sale of medical products, government regulation, geopolitical conflicts, changing global trade policies, general economic conditions, and other risks and uncertainties described in the company’s filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. In some cases, you can identify these statements by forward-looking words or expressions, such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “forecast,” “intend,” “looking ahead,” “may,” “plan,” “possible,” “potential,” “project,” “should,” “going to,” “will,” and similar words or expressions, the negative or plural of such words or expressions and other comparable terminology. Actual results may differ materially from anticipated results. MiniMed does not undertake to update its forward-looking statements or any of the information contained in this press release, including to reflect future events or circumstances. 
 About MiniMed
 MiniMed is a global leader in insulin delivery, constantly advancing therapies that support people with diabetes in more than 80 countries. Our full-stack, integrated ecosystem, including our insulin delivery systems, CGMs, algorithms, and easy-to-use app experience, is designed to work seamlessly together, supported by white-glove, wrap-around service. For over 40 years, we’ve pioneered therapies people can rely on by anticipating needs, reducing burden, and helping make life with diabetes easier. Our mission is to make every day a better day for people with diabetes.

This includes Organic Revenue Growth, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin and Free Cash Flow. We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide information useful to investors in understanding our underlying operational performance, liquidity, trends and our ability to generate cash from operations after investments in property, plant and equipment and may facilitate comparisons with the performance of other companies in the medical technologies industry.
